author: blu
body: The second partition carries the FACT STORE type GUID and not the generic basic-data one. That is what DiskFacts looks for, and it is the whole difference between a stick that can persist a fact and one where the store refuses because it can find no region of its own. It was basic-data while the store addressed absolute sectors, which is to say while it could not use a partition at all.

author: blu
body: So this is one function, it is the one the menu calls, and it says which link failed rather than answering a bare Boolean. The old one discarded the result of the copy and returned True regardless, which is the reading that would have hidden all of this the moment the drives became real.

author: blu
body: The source is read through whichever filesystem its ESP actually carries. A stick built by `build-boot-img.ps1` is FAT16; one built with `-Fat32`, or any volume past 2 GB, is not. Assuming either one is how the dead path stayed plausible.

author: blu
body: A stick that boots and cannot verify or rebuild itself is not what this project promises anyone, so the install carries the seed and the source text as well as the boot image. The boot image is required and its absence refuses the install; the other two are copied when the source has them, because a machine installing from a stick that was itself built without them should still get a bootable target rather than nothing.

author: blu
body: The source is read BEFORE the target is touched. Partitioning first and discovering afterwards that there is nothing to install leaves the target wiped, which is the worst answer available: the old inline path did exactly that.

author: blu
body: `fat32-write-file` walks the path and creates the directories it needs, so the mkdir-then-find-then-mkdir dance both installers performed was redundant. It was also the thing that failed: it is the older interface, from before `fat32-ensure-parent-dirs` existed, and nothing had run it since.
